title: Naturality and finite coefficient scalar compatibility of the prescribed rational Koszul braiding
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $W$ any scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field. For every finite coefficient subfield $E\subset\Omega$, use the raw rational constructible category $C_E=D^b_c(W,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] (objects are integral derived-complete bounded constructible objects and Hom modules are localized, without Karoubi completion), its tensor $T_E$, and its normalized tensor scalar comparisons [def-sf-finite-rational-derived-operations]. For $E\subset L$, write $F_{EL}:C_E\to C_L$ for the prescribed rational scalar extension [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and $\lambda_{EL;A,B}:F_{EL}T_E(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_L(F_{EL}A,F_{EL}B)$ for this specific comparison. Let $\sigma^E_{A,B}:T_E(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_E(B,A)$ be the prescribed rational Koszul braiding [def-sf-rational-common-tensor-symmetries]: the localization of the coherent-reduction-normalized integral Koszul braiding [def-pod-integral-tensor-constraints], using the specified tensor-object identifications. These isomorphisms form a natural isomorphism $T_E\cong T_E\circ\mathrm{swap}$. Explicitly, for arbitrary localized arrows $a:A\to A'$ and $b:B\to B'$,
$$\sigma^E_{A',B'}\circ T_E(a,b)=T_E(b,a)\circ\sigma^E_{A,B}.$$
For every $E\subset L$ and every $A,B\in C_E$, including identity and ramified extensions, the prescribed scalar comparison satisfies
$$\lambda_{EL;B,A}\circ F_{EL}(\sigma^E_{A,B})=\sigma^L_{F_{EL}A,F_{EL}B}\circ\lambda_{EL;A,B}.$$
No finite-field structure on $W$, perfectness of the inputs, or torsion-freeness of Hom modules is assumed.

proof.text: The coherently reduction-normalized integral Koszul braiding is natural by [lem-pur-integral-braiding-naturality]. Its proof checks the equality after coherent reduction, where both composites on homogeneous terms $x$ of degree $i$ and $y$ of degree $j$ are the signed exchange $(-1)^{ij}(b(y)\otimes a(x))$; full faithfulness of coherent reduction then lifts the equality. Thus the integral equation used below has exactly the displayed source and target.

proof.text:
For localized arrows $a$ and $b$, write them as finite sums of pure tensors of integral arrows with scalar coefficients. By the rational operation formulas of [def-sf-finite-rational-derived-operations] and the definition of $\sigma^E$ as the localization of the integral braiding in [def-sf-rational-common-tensor-symmetries], both sides of
$$\sigma^E_{A',B'}\circ T_E(a,b)=T_E(b,a)\circ\sigma^E_{A,B}$$
are the corresponding scalar multiples of the integral equation from Step 1. Additivity and the balancing relation in the raw localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] extend the equality from pure tensors to all localized arrows. This proves the first clause, including identities and zero morphisms.

proof.text: Let $E\subset L$ and $A,B\in C_E$. The objects of $C_E$ are integral objects, $F_{EL}$ is the integral scalar extension $K\mapsto K_L$ on objects and $f\otimes c\mapsto f_L\otimes c$ on morphisms [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and on integral representatives the prescribed comparison $\lambda_{EL;A,B}$ is the localization $\lambda^{\mathrm{int}}_{A,B}\otimes1$ of the prescribed integral tensor scalar comparison [def-sf-finite-rational-derived-operations]. By [def-sf-rational-common-tensor-symmetries], $\sigma^E_{A,B}$ and $\sigma^L_{F_{EL}A,F_{EL}B}$ are the localizations $\beta^E_{A,B}\otimes1$ and $\beta^L_{A_L,B_L}\otimes1$ of the coherent-reduction-normalized integral braidings [def-pod-integral-tensor-constraints], with the same tensor objects. Hence $F_{EL}(\sigma^E_{A,B})=(\beta^E_{A,B})_L\otimes1$, and since composition in the raw localization is $(u\otimes c)\circ(v\otimes d)=(u\circ v)\otimes cd$, the two sides of the asserted square are $(\lambda^{\mathrm{int}}_{B,A}\circ(\beta^E_{A,B})_L)\otimes1$ and $(\beta^L_{A_L,B_L}\circ\lambda^{\mathrm{int}}_{A,B})\otimes1$. These integral composites are equal by [lem-pur-integral-braiding-scalar-extension-square], for every finite $E\subset L$, including $L=E$ and ramified extensions. Only object components occur in this square, so no extension over arbitrary localized arrows is needed; no unramifiedness, perfectness or torsion-freeness is used.
